body.statement:
Let \(\mathfrak Q_{\mathrm{src}}(P^{\circ})\) be the published Assumptions 1--4 completion class and let \(Q_c^{\circ}\) be the affine completion generated by \(c\in\mathbb R\) and \(\phi\). The law \(P^{\circ}\) has a bounded density that is strictly positive on each rectangle of its finite rectangle support and has uniformly bounded observed outcomes. It satisfies marginal quasi-stayers, whereas baseline-conditional positivity fails for every \(x\in[-1,0)\), a region of \(P^{\circ}_X\)-probability \(p_{\circ}\). For every finite \(c\), \(Q_c^{\circ}\in\mathfrak Q_{\mathrm{src}}(P^{\circ})\), its schedules are affine and integrable, it preserves the entire observed law, and it satisfies parallel trends simultaneously for every \(d\in[-2,2]\). Moreover,
\[
\theta(Q_c^{\circ})=-\frac{3c p_{\circ}}{1+5p_{\circ}},
\qquad
\{\theta(Q):Q\in\mathfrak Q_{\mathrm{src}}(P^{\circ})\}=\mathbb R.
\]
For the strengthened sensitivity class with \(K=L=M=1\), \(Q_+^{\circ}=Q_1^{\circ}\) and \(Q_-^{\circ}=Q_{-1}^{\circ}\) attain the endpoints
\[
\Theta(P^{\circ})=
\left[-\frac{3p_{\circ}}{1+5p_{\circ}},
       \frac{3p_{\circ}}{1+5p_{\circ}}\right].
\]
Thus the identification elbow has three distinct stages: the unrestricted published class gives all of \(\mathbb R\) at this regular witness; the bounded-slope/Lipschitz class gives the displayed finite obstacle interval; and, under baseline-conditional zero support, the obstacle restriction fixes \(u(x)=g(x,0)\) and yields the published weighted singleton formula. Only the negative conclusion for the published singleton transfers to the published class; the finite interval does not.
body.proof_tex:
The first rectangle in the definition of \(P^{\circ}\) has area \(1/2\) and density \(2p_{\circ}\), so it has probability \(p_{\circ}\). The second also has area \(1/2\) and has density \(2(1-p_{\circ})\), so it has probability \(1-p_{\circ}\). Since \(p_{\circ}\in(0,1)\), the density is bounded and strictly positive on each of the two rectangles. The observed outcomes are zero and hence uniformly bounded. Absolute continuity gives \(P^{\circ}(Z=0)=0\). The second rectangle contains treatment changes arbitrarily close to zero with positive Lebesgue measure, and therefore
\[
P^{\circ}(|Z|\leq\eta)>0\qquad\text{for every }\eta>0.
\]
In contrast, for every \(x\in[-1,0)\), the conditional support of \(Z\) is \([1/2,1]\), whence
\[
P^{\circ}(|Z|\leq\eta\mid X=x)=0
\qquad\text{for }0<\eta<1/2.
\]
The marginal density of \(X\) on \([-1,0]\) is \(p_{\circ}\), so the failure region has \(P_X^{\circ}\)-probability \(p_{\circ}\).

Fix a finite \(c\in\mathbb R\). On the first rectangle, \(|\phi(X)|\leq1/2\leq |Z|\), while on the second rectangle \(\phi(X)=0\). Thus, off the null event \(\{Z=0\}\),
\[
\left|\frac{c\phi(X)}{Z}\right|\leq |c|.
\]
Because \(D_1,D_2,d\in[-2,2]\), both schedules in the definition of \(Q_c^{\circ}\) are bounded in absolute value by \(4|c|\) for every fixed \(d\). They are therefore integrable, affine in \(d\), and have everywhere finite slope. At the realized treatments,
\[
Y_1^{Q_c^{\circ}}(D_1)=0=Y_1,
\qquad
Y_2^{Q_c^{\circ}}(D_2)=0=Y_2.
\]
Consequently consistency holds and the complete observed vector retains law \(P^{\circ}\).

For every \(d\in[-2,2]\), direct subtraction gives, on the same event for all \(d\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
Y_2^{Q_c^{\circ}}(d)-Y_1^{Q_c^{\circ}}(d)
&=-\frac{c\phi(X)}{Z}\{(d-D_2)-(d-X)\}\\
&=c\phi(X).
\end{aligned}
\]
The right-hand side is measurable with respect to \(X\). Hence
\[
E_{Q_c^{\circ}}[Y_2^{Q_c^{\circ}}(d)-Y_1^{Q_c^{\circ}}(d)\mid X,Z]
=c\phi(X)
=E_{Q_c^{\circ}}[Y_2^{Q_c^{\circ}}(d)-Y_1^{Q_c^{\circ}}(d)\mid X]
\]
simultaneously for every \(d\). This verifies the source parallel-trends clause, and in fact its stronger common-event version. The observed support clauses were verified above, so \(Q_c^{\circ}\in\mathfrak Q_{\mathrm{src}}(P^{\circ})\).

The period-two causal movement is
\[
Y_2^{Q_c^{\circ}}(D_2)-Y_2^{Q_c^{\circ}}(D_1)
=-c\phi(X).
\]
On the first rectangle \(S=1\). On the second rectangle, \(Z\) is conditionally uniform on the symmetric interval \([-1/4,1/4]\), and \(\phi(X)=0\) there in any event. Therefore
\[
E_{P^{\circ}}[S\phi(X)]
=p_{\circ}\int_{-1}^0\min\{-x,1/2\}\,dx
=\frac{3p_{\circ}}8.
\]
Also,
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_{P^{\circ}}|Z|
&=p_{\circ}\,E[Z\mid Z\in[1/2,1]]
 +(1-p_{\circ})E[|Z|\mid Z\in[-1/4,1/4]]\\
&=\frac{3p_{\circ}}4+\frac{1-p_{\circ}}8
=\frac{1+5p_{\circ}}8.
\end{aligned}
\]
It follows from the causal definition, rather than by definition of an observed functional, that
\[
\theta(Q_c^{\circ})
=\frac{-cE_{P^{\circ}}[S\phi(X)]}{E_{P^{\circ}}|Z|}
=-\frac{3cp_{\circ}}{1+5p_{\circ}}.
\]
The multiplier \(3p_{\circ}/(1+5p_{\circ})\) is strictly positive. As \(c\) ranges over \(\mathbb R\), these values range over all of \(\mathbb R\), proving
\[
\mathbb R\subseteq
\{\theta(Q):Q\in\mathfrak Q_{\mathrm{src}}(P^{\circ})\}.
\]
The reverse inclusion is immediate from the definition of the source completion class, which requires the causal movement defining \(\theta(Q)\) to be integrable, so every \(\theta(Q)\) is a finite real number. This proves equality.

It remains to calculate the middle, bounded-sensitivity stage. Because \(\Delta Y=0\), the continuous support version is \(g=0\). For \(K=L=M=1\), every \(u\in\mathcal C_{P^{\circ}}\) obeys \(u(x)=0\) on \([0,1]\), since \((x,0)\in H\) there. On \([-1,0]\), the support contains \((x,1/2)\), so the obstacle restriction gives \(|u(x)|\leq1/2\). Global one-Lipschitz continuity and \(u(0)=0\) also give \(|u(x)|\leq -x\). Hence
\[
|u(x)|\leq\phi(x)\qquad\text{for every }x\in[-1,1].
\]
Both \(\phi\) and \(-\phi\) are continuous, bounded by one, globally one-Lipschitz, and satisfy every support obstacle, so both belong to \(\mathcal C_{P^{\circ}}\).

On the first rectangle \(S=1\), whereas on the second rectangle the conditional sign mean is zero. It follows that
\[
d\nu_{P^{\circ}}(x)
=p_{\circ}\mathbf 1\{x\in[-1,0]\}\,dx.
\]
Consequently
\[
-\frac{3p_{\circ}}8
\leq J_{P^{\circ}}(u)
\leq\frac{3p_{\circ}}8,
\]
and the two bounds are attained by \(-\phi\) and \(\phi\), respectively. Since \(T=0\) and \(A=(1+5p_{\circ})/8\), full-law sharpness and the attained-interval theorem give
\[
\Theta(P^{\circ})
=\left[-\frac{3p_{\circ}}{1+5p_{\circ}},
        \frac{3p_{\circ}}{1+5p_{\circ}}\right].
\]
The definitions show \(Q_+^{\circ}=Q_1^{\circ}\) and \(Q_-^{\circ}=Q_{-1}^{\circ}\), so these two completions attain the lower and upper endpoints, respectively.

Finally, if baseline-conditional zero support is imposed so that \((x,0)\in H\) at every relevant baseline \(x\), the defining obstacle at \((x,0)\) reads
\[
|g(x,0)-u(x)|\leq K|0|=0.
\]
Thus every compatible \(u\) equals the observed trend \(g(\cdot,0)\), and the bounded-class set reduces to
\[
\left\{\frac{T-\int_{X_0}g(x,0)\,d\nu_P(x)}{A}\right\}.
\]
This proves the stated three-stage elbow and also shows why the finite sensitivity interval cannot be promoted to the unrestricted published completion class.
body.justification: The affine recession ray proves that the published-class failure is unbounded, while the bounded-slope/Lipschitz model has a finite sharp interval.
body.gap: Marginal quasi-stayers do not supply the baseline-conditional support used before display (4) in the proof of the published theorem; the regular witness makes the resulting source-class identified set equal to \(\mathbb R\).
body.consumer: The result separates the invalid published singleton, the finite sensitivity interval under explicit bounds, and recovery of the weighted singleton under conditional zero support.
